head: pr17421-r17
report:
I found three defects to fix before merge. All are in the new Python bridge fallback: the "standing" per-session entry. I ran a probe for #1. #2 and #3 come from reading the code; I didn't measure them. I skipped most of the session-manager, artifact-staging and main.ts changes because of the time limit. In what I did read there, the ownership probe and refcounted snapshot claims looked sound.

## 1. Python bridge runs any tool for a stale or made-up run id (the "Missing run" check can be bypassed)

**Where:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts`, in `startServer` → `fetch` (around lines 195–199 of the snapshot), and `registerPyToolBridge`.

**How it happens:** `registerPyToolBridge` now also writes every entry into `sessionRegistrations[sessionId]`, and the returned `unregister` never removes it. The lookup became
`registrations.get(`${sessionId}:${runId}`) ?? sessionRegistrations.get(sessionId)`.
The new gate only rejects an **empty** `run`, and only for names other than `__artifacts_ready__`. A request that sends any non-empty run id therefore passes the gate and falls through to the standing entry, whatever tool it names. That includes a cell that already finished, or a run id that never existed. Before this change, the old fallback `registrations.get(sessionId)` never matched, because keys are always `sid:rid`. Such calls got `No active Python tool bridge session`.

The code comment says "Everything else still has to say which cell it is". The code does not enforce that.

**Real-world trigger:** In cell 1, `asyncio.create_task(...)` a coroutine that calls `tool.bash(...)` or `agent(...)` after the cell returns. Asyncio tasks inherit contextvars, so `__omp_current_run_id__` still returns cell 1's rid. That call now runs:
- with the most recent cell's `ToolSession`, `signal`, `shieldedSignal` and `emitStatus`;
- even after every cell has ended;
- with its status attributed to a later cell, outside that cell's abort and accounting.

**Repro:** `py-bridge-stale-run.test.ts` in the scratch directory. It calls `registerPyToolBridge("sess-A","run-1",…)`, calls `unregister()` (the cell ended), then POSTs `/v1/tool` three times. Measured result:
```
{"stale":{"ok":true,"value":"RAN"},"forged":{"ok":true,"value":"RAN"},"empty":{"ok":false,"error":"Missing run"},"calls":2}
```
The tool ran for both the stale run id `run-1` and the forged run id `anything`. Only an empty run id is refused.

**Fix:** Look up `sessionRegistrations` only when `name === EVAL_ARTIFACTS_READY_BRIDGE_NAME`. Every other name must match a live `sid:rid` entry.

## 2. `sessionRegistrations` leaks a `ToolSession` per per-call execution, and is never cleared

**How it happens:** The only call to `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession` is in `shutdownInvalidatedSession` (session-mode kernels). Per-call mode is different:
- `executePerCall` mints `bridgeSessionId = py-bridge:${randomUUID()}` for each execution.
- `executor-base.ts:500` registers it.
- The kernel is then shut down directly with `kernel.shutdown()`.

So every per-call Python cell leaves one entry in the module-level map, holding a `ToolSession`, its `AbortSignal`s and an `emitStatus` closure, for the life of the process. `disposePyToolBridge` clears only `registrations`, not `sessionRegistrations`, so even the shutdown/test helper leaves them behind. Combined with #1, those leaked entries still answer tool calls for their bridge session id.

**Trigger:** Run Python eval in `per-call` kernel mode N times. `sessionRegistrations.size` grows by N and never shrinks.

## 3. Shutting down one Python kernel removes the standing entry other kernels of the same session depend on

**How it happens:** Session-mode kernels are keyed by `sessionId\0cwd\0interpreter`, but `bridgeSessionId` is just `sessionId` (`kernel-session-registry.ts:431`). So kernels for different cwds or interpreters share one `sessionRegistrations` slot. When `shutdownInvalidatedSession` runs for kernel A (reset, invalidation or idle shutdown), it calls `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession(sessionId)`. That deletes the entry that kernel B's latest cell installed.

A background thread in B (no run id, so routed to the standing entry) that reads `artifact://N` then gets `No active Python tool bridge session`. In the same way, a thread in A can be answered with B's entry while both are alive.

**Trigger:** Keep two Python kernels alive in one session (different `cwd`). Leave a `threading.Thread` in B that later reads `artifact://1`. Reset A, and B's background read fails.

## Lesser: a Python `artifact://N` read now fails with no tool bridge, where it used to work

`_artifact_file` used to list the artifacts directory locally. Now it always goes through `_bridge_call("__artifacts_ready__", …)`, and `_tool_proxy_from_env` raises `RuntimeError("tool bridge is unavailable in this kernel")` when `PI_TOOL_BRIDGE_*` is unset. That happens, for example, when `ensureToolBridge` failed: it only logs a warning and continues. The case that regressed is when this session's artifact exists locally: `read("artifact://N")` now raises instead of reading the file. I did not reproduce this; it comes from reading the code.
